description: In the 5th century BC, Athens invented a system where citizens governed directly. Lottery draw, equal say… and massive exclusion.

hero.hook: How a Greek city invented the power of the people, and its limits.

blocks.text: In the 5th century BC, Athens invented something radical: the **[[policy]]** in the sense that citizens were no longer subjects of a king, but actors of their destiny. Power (*kratos*) belongs to the people (*demos*). Hence the word democracy.
This direct democracy, born from crises and reforms, remains a reference for Western political thought, with its strengths and its blind spots.

In the 7th century BC, Athens was torn between aristocrats and indebted peasants. , statesman elected in **594 BC.**, abolishes debt slavery and opens magistracies according to fortune, not just blood. **[[Solon]]**

The real turning point is (**508-507**). This reformer created **10 mixed tribes** to break up the clans, and established the **[[Cleisthenes]]**, Council of Five Hundred drawn by lot. Every citizen can serve the city. **[[Boule]]**

blocks.caption: The Agora of Athens, heart of civic life.

blocks.text: To remove a man who was too powerful, the Athenians voted the **[[Ostracism]]** on a ceramic shard: ten-year exile, with a quorum of **6, 000** voters.

sections.title: Reforms that open up the city

blocks.text: In the middle of the 5th century, under **Pericles**, a strategist re-elected fifteen times and a figure of the Athenian golden age, the system became more open. The **Ecclesia**, citizens' assembly, meets approximately **40 times** per year on the hill of the Pnyx. She votes on laws, war, peace, the budget.

blocks.caption: Pericles, strategist re-elected fifteen times, figure of the Athenian golden age.

blocks.text: The **[[Helie]]** guarantees equality of speech. The **[[Isegoria]]**, daily allowance, allows the poorest to sit. Justice passes through the **[[Misthos]]**: **6 000** jurors drawn by lot. The drawing of lots limits the monopolization of power, except for military strategists.

Out of approximately **300,000** residents, only **30,000 to 50,000** male citizens vote. Women, slaves and metics (resident foreigners) are excluded. In **451**, Pericles even toughens the rule: two citizen parents are required.
Founding paradox: equality between peers is based on slavery and exclusion. A face-to-face democracy, intense, but closed.
Anyone who was disinterested in public life was called *idiots* (“individual”). The word gave “idiot”: cutting oneself off from the common good was seen as a lack of reason.

A [[Demagogue]], a speaker who flatters the passions, can carry the assembly with emotion. **Plato**, philosopher marked by the death of his master **Socrates** (**399 BC**), sees in democracy the reign of opinion against the truth, and the typical example of the tyranny of the majority.

Despite its flaws, Athens bequeaths lasting ideas: responsibility of those in power, equality before the law, contradictory debate. Today, drawing lots and direct democracy even come up in contemporary discussions.

Athenian democracy was a direct government of free male citizens, based on drawing lots and equality of speech. It excluded approximately **85%** of the population, but invented Western public debate.
